prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Prototype Controller Board BOM (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Part number" · longest unbreakable word 165px · one-line width 165px
  col 2: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 107px · one-line width 526px
  col 3: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 4: header "Unit price" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 70px
  col 5: header "Supplier" · longest unbreakable word 133px · one-line width 133px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Identify and source the parts needed to build a prototype controller board, with quantities and unit prices.","reading":"Readers locate a part by number or description, then scan across its row to check quantity, price and supplier. The descriptions are much longer than the other values, so their wrapping will largely determine row height.","groups":["Part number and description identify the component and its specifications.","Quantity and unit price support purchasing and cost comparisons.","Supplier complements the part number as a sourcing reference."],"keep_intact":["Part numbers and supplier names, especially long unbreakable identifiers.","Quantities and unit-price values, so they remain easy to compare."],"may_wrap":["Descriptions can wrap at spaces; shorter cells in the same row can occupy the resulting height.","The Unit price header can wrap if the price values remain readable."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [186, 252, 47, 80, 154] · table 720×500px · row heights [60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Part numbers, quantities, prices and supplier names remain intact, making each row easy to scan across. The description receives most of the flexible width, and its wrapping creates a consistent rhythm across most rows.","problems":"The Unit price header wraps onto two lines, making the header row taller and giving that short purchasing column more visual weight than it needs. The microcontroller description takes three lines, while the ESD description breaks the hyphenated term “2-line” across lines.","cause":"The 80px price column provides 59px for text, less than the header’s 70px one-line width. The 252px description column provides 231px for text, so longer descriptions wrap at available break points."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"single-line-price-header","widths":[186,241,47,91,154],"change":"Give Unit price 11px more so its header fits on one line, taking that space from Description.
